tweets.text:
I think this is a very fair way of looking at it! My perception is that Zcash is winning the privacy narrative because it has the best tech. Any crack in its architecture is maybe even more damaging to its value than the less sophisticated privacy protocols out there, because suddenly it's not the perfect solution anymore.
It's true that it would still be a viable blockchain with a great development community underneath, but losing its USP would be severe in my eyes and that is why I have adjusted my risk. I do expect there will be others out there who do not take that view, but that is any speculative market; it is an aggregate of all of these understandings. If you have read my other writings you will know I am no longer a fan of Bitcoin (and its "money" narrative) given its current state. This is also why I have encouraged ZSAs to be implemented. Onchain revenue and anonymity sets are two very important moats for a protocol's standing in the industry.
